description: The built-in proof of work of the Interaction API's captcha step, whose params are provider pow, a challenge and a difficulty: whether a captcha_token solves the puzzle. input.challenge is the step's challenge (base64url text), input.difficulty its difficulty (1 to 32) and input.captcha_token the answer. expected.digest is the SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the challenge, a colon and the token (<challenge>:<captcha_token>), with the challenge as the text it is, not decoded; it is base64url without padding. expected.leading_zero_bits is how many bits of that digest are zero before its first one bit, reading the first byte first and each byte from its most significant bit. expected.accepted is true only when captcha_token is a nonce, that is one to 16 ASCII digits 0 to 9 with no sign and no leading zero (0 itself is a nonce), and leading_zero_bits is at least difficulty. expected.smallest_solution is true only when the token is accepted and no smaller nonce is: the nonce a solver that tries 0, 1, 2 and so on returns. digest and leading_zero_bits are given for every token, so a case refused for its form shows that its digest alone would have passed.
source: The captcha step of the Interaction API v1-rc.0 contract (#643, #1082); generated by test-vectors/generators/proof-of-work.mjs with Node.js node:crypto

cases.notes: The challenge is hashed as the text it is: its base64url is not decoded first. The reference solver tries 0, 1, 2 and so on, and returns this nonce.

The example of the captcha step in the Interaction API contract (/interaction/v1-rc.0/openapi.json): its params and its answer. Until QAuth 1.0.0 this case follows the example, as interaction/steps.json does.
Exactly 12 leading zero bits pass a difficulty of 12. It is a larger solution than the smallest one, and any solution passes.
11 leading zero bits do not pass a difficulty of 12.
The digest's first byte is 0x01: seven zero bits before the first one bit, read from the most significant bit.
The digest's first byte is 0x80: its first bit is one, so it has no leading zero bit, though its seven least significant bits are zero.
0 is a nonce: the one nonce that starts with the digit 0.
The longest nonce, 16 digits, past the largest integer a JavaScript number holds exactly: a solver that counts in doubles never reaches it.
Its digest would pass; 17 digits are one too many.
Its digest would pass; a nonce other than 0 does not start with the digit 0.
Its digest would pass; a nonce has no sign.

Its digest would pass; a line feed is not a digit. A pattern whose end anchor also matches before a final line feed, as `$` does in Python, PCRE and Perl, takes it: match the whole string. On the wire the answer schema (printable ASCII) refuses it first, as an invalid answer.

Its digest would pass; Arabic-Indic digits match \d in some pattern engines, Python's and .NET's among them, but a nonce is ASCII 0 to 9. On the wire the answer schema (printable ASCII) refuses it first, as an invalid answer.
